## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This review found only optional corrections in the reviewed scope: `test_rejects_legacy_header` cannot fail for the version check it names. `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already guards the exact-match header check at `app/report.py:5`.

## Changes
The pull request makes `parse_report` accept only an exact `REPORT v1` header instead of any line starting with `REPORT `, and it adds two rejection tests.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — Make the legacy-header test reach the version check — The fixture `"REPORT v1\nversion=v1"` has no `END` line, and `rsplit` turns it into `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`, which keeps the `v1` header. `parse_report` returns `None` at the `END` check on `app/report.py:3`, so the test passes even with the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check. The comment on line 9 says the test changes "the fixture's version to v0", but the code changes only a body value. — This test protects nothing despite its name and comment, so a reader could think legacy headers are covered twice. — Fix: Use a complete report with a `REPORT v0` header, or delete the test because `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that case.
